title: QBR: Adaptive Bite-Sized Deck Templates & Renewal Sprint Tracker (Draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact, modular QBR deck kit plus a lightweight renewal sprint tracker meant for Customer Success teams who want a short, repeatable format that scales from small accounts to enterprise relationships. Draft is intentionally "bite-sized" — main goal: reduce prep time, force prioritization, and give a clear renewal path for each cohort.

Intended audience:
- CSMs leading 30–60 minute quarterly business reviews
- AMs prepping enterprise exec briefings (use the enterprise variation chapters)
- Renewal managers looking for a unified tracker and handoff checklist

How to use this kit (quick start):
1) Choose the deck length: 10 slides = standard (30–40 min), 16 slides = enterprise (45–60+ min).
2) Pull pre-read metrics 72 hours before the meeting (usage, spend, latency, error rate, adoption signals).
3) Share the one‑page executive snapshot as pre-read.
4) Run the meeting with the timebox per slide below.
5) Capture actions in the renewal sprint tracker and assign owners within 48 hours.

Pre-work checklist (CSM):
- Confirm attendees and exec level owner.
- Export last 90-day usage and last 30-day trends.
- Identify 2 wins and 2 risks for the account.
- Draft 1–2 recommendations with potential business impact (token savings, latency improvements, reliability mitigations).

Slide templates and speaker notes (standard deck, 10-slide):
Slide 0: Title + Meeting logistics (2 min)
- Title: Account QBR / Customer name / Quarter + Date
- Notes: confirm agenda and alignment at start

Slide 1: Executive snapshot (3 min)
- One-line description of customer objective, ARR band, and strategic importance
- Top-line metrics: MRR/ARR impact, usage growth %, renewal date
- Speaker note: this is the single slide execs read if they skip the rest

Slide 2: Health score & trends (4 min)
- Metric components: usage, latency, error rate, feature adoption, support volume
- Show 3-month sparkline and current score.
- Quick callout: root cause for any >10% drop

Slide 3: Adoption highlights (4 min)
- Top 3 product features in use, sticky workflows, reference customer activity
- Quote or short CSAT snippet if available

Slide 4: Cost & efficiency snapshot (4 min)
- Current spend trends, per-call cost, quantization/batching opportunities
- Suggested quick wins (e.g., enable prefix caching, reduce max tokens)

Slide 5: Reliability and incidents (3 min)
- Recent incidents, P95 latency, SLI gaps
- Mitigation plan and recommended changes (routing, fallback model)

Slide 6: Open product requests & roadmap fit (3 min)
- Map of top 2 customer asks to Redwood roadmap items
- Ask: decide priority for next quarter

Slide 7: Renewal health and risk indicators (3 min)
- Renewal date, NPS/CSAT trends, contract terms, expansion pipeline
- Risk flags: new competing pilots, exec churn, contract threshold misses

Slide 8: Proposed next-quarter plan (5 min)
- Concrete goals (e.g., reduce cost per inference by 20%, 2x active users)
- Three initiatives with owners and success metrics

Slide 9: Decisions & actions (3 min)
- Confirm next steps, owners, target dates, and where decisions are blocked

Enterprise variation (16-slide) — additions and changes:
- Add a 1-page compliance and security appendix (KMS/HSM, data residency)
- Expand the usage section into per-team or per-workload breakdowns
- Add a deep-dive appendix on latency budgets and fallback policies
- Insert a commercial section with renewal terms, pricing sensitivity analysis, and proposed contract options (renewal, expansion, committed spend)
- Timebox: add a 10-minute executive Q&A and a 15-minute technical break-out for SRE/engineering stakeholders

Commercial scripts and negotiation playbook (bulleted prompts):
- If renewal risk = low: focus on expansion opportunities and business outcomes; present pricing incrementally tied to committed throughput.
- If renewal risk = medium: propose short-term extension + 60–90 day action plan; offer technical support time to address performance blockers.
- If renewal risk = high: propose a phased renewal with opt-out triggers linked to agreed SLAs; escalate to AE with a combined CSM/AE bridge meeting.

Renewal sprint tracker (lightweight format) — fields to capture:
- Account name (string)
- Renewal date (date string)
- Current ARR / committed spend (string)
- Renewal owner (CSM or AE name)
- Risk level (low|medium|high)
- Top 3 blockers (list as comma-separated string)
- Actions (list of short strings)
- Owner for each action (string)
- Due date for each action (date string)
- Status (open|in_progress|done)
- Notes (freeform string)

Tracker usage guidance:
- Keep tracker short; aim for 5–8 active actions per account max.
- Update after every key touchpoint; required update cadence = twice weekly for medium/high risk.
- Use the tracker to generate a weekly renewal pulse report for GTM leadership.

Handoff checklist (CSM -> AE / Renewal team):
- Attach the last two QBR decks and the tracker export.
- Confirm approved commercial levers and boundaries.
- Technical mitigations and SLO commitments documented with SRE contact.
- Exec sponsor contact info and preferred communication cadence.

Sample action labels (for consistent reporting):
- TECH_FIX: incident mitigation or configuration change
- PRODUCT_REQUEST: backlog item to prioritize
- COMMERCIAL_OFFER: pricing/term negotiation action
- ENG_ALIGN: engineering deep-dive requested
- EXEC_SYNC: executive alignment meeting scheduled

Metrics collection notes (data pulls for pre-read):
- Usage: 90-day unique calls, 30-day trend, top 5 endpoints by volume
- Cost: token consumption per endpoint, per-request P95 cost estimate
- Performance: P50/P95 latency, dropped requests, error categories
- Support: open tickets by severity and time to first response
- Business: ARR, MRR, recent upsells, proof points for ROI

Runbook for risk escalations (short):
- Day 0 (post-QBR): assign actions and set owner deadlines in tracker.
- Day 3: CSM triage; escalate technical blockers to SRE with severity tag.
- Day 7: AE engaged for commercial blockers.
- Day 14: Exec sponsor sync scheduled if risk remains high.

Open questions and TODOs (draft stage):
- Add a compact slide template for partner integrations (APIs, webhooks) — needed?
- Build a Jira template for automated tracker creation and reminders.
- Define exact formula for the health score (weighting of metrics).
- Validate enterprise pricing sensitivity examples with finance.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally frugal: the idea is to force decisions and action rather than produce long decks.
- We experimented with a 6-slide ultra-sprint QBR for expansion ops; it works for small accounts but fails to surface technical risks for enterprise.
- Feedback requested: 1) health score weighting, 2) columns to include in tracker export, 3) whether to standardize the commercial scripts per ARR band.

Appendix (examples and snippets):
- Sample one-line exec snapshot: "Customer: Acme Corp — Platform payments vertical; QTD spend +18%; Renewal 2025-05-18; Ask: reduce inference costs and increase throughput for peak events."
- Sample action row: Account=Acme, Action=Enable KV prefix caching in prod, Owner=Hannah Cho, Due=2024-11-20, Status=in_progress

Revision history and provenance:
- Drafted by Priya Nair on 2024-11-02.
- Added tracker fields and enterprise appendix after input from Marco and Avery on 2024-12-08.
- Current draft updated 2025-01-15 with negotiation scripts and runbook steps.

End of document.
